references.text: The commandment about tassels (tsitsit) on the corners of the garment – the Greek word 'kraspedon' (κράσπεδον) refers to these tassels/fringes on the garment, which Jesus wore in accordance with the Mosaic Law.
The law's provisions regarding a woman with prolonged bleeding – she was unclean according to the law, making her touching of Jesus' garment even more remarkable.
Matthew's parallel account of the woman with bleeding who touched the edge of Jesus' garment and was healed.
Mark's parallel account of the same event, with additional details about the woman's suffering and immediate healing.
People asked to touch the edge (kraspedon) of Jesus' garment, and all who touched it were healed – the same theme of healing power through touching the tassel of the garment.
Wherever Jesus went, the sick asked to touch the edge of his garment, and all who touched it were healed.
The prophecy that the sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings – 'wings' (kanaf) can also mean the corner/fringe of a garment, linking healing to the edge of the garment.
God's power worked unusual miracles through Paul, so that even cloths and handkerchiefs from him healed the sick – parallel to healing power working through physical touch or objects.
